meta.name: Urban Nature Explorer
meta.author: OUTSIDE//OS Core Team & Hacktoberfest Contributors
meta.description: Discover resilient ecology flourishing within cities, pavement crevices, stone walls, and neighborhood alleyways.
safety_guidelines: Stay strictly on designated public pedestrian walkways.
Never enter private easements or construction zones.
Do not step into bicycle lanes or street gutters without checking for traffic.
Do not touch sharp building debris, glass, or discarded waste.

quests.title: Sidewalk Crack Flora Cartography
quests.objective: Catalog three species of resilient spontaneous plants thriving in pavement margins or brick seams.
quests.suitability_reason: Ideal for urban pedestrians with 15 minutes to spare. No park or forest required; any city sidewalk qualifies.

steps.instruction: Step out onto your street and follow a pedestrian sidewalk for 20 paces.
steps.detail: Keep phone stored away; direct your gaze down to the seams between concrete flags.

steps.instruction: Find the first pioneer plant emerging from a crack or curb foundation.
steps.detail: Observe its root anchoring mechanism and leaf shape (e.g. dandelion rosette, plantain, or clover).

steps.instruction: Locate two additional distinct specimens along your route without picking them.
steps.detail: Notice which one shows signs of vehicle exhaust resistance or foot-traffic tolerance.

checklist: Identified a plant flourishing in an asphalt or concrete seam
Noticed moisture accumulation or micro-soil trapped in the crack
quests.bonus_challenge: Spot an ant or tiny beetle using the crack as a travel corridor.
quests.safe_alternative: Observe street tree pits or window planter boxes from your doorstep or building foyer.
quests.completion_criteria: Find at least two surviving wild plants in human-made joints.
quests.reflection_question: What does the tenacity of these crack-dwelling plants reveal about nature in built environments?
safety_notes: Never kneel or crouch directly in vehicle roadways or bike lanes.
Be aware of other pedestrians passing by.

quests.title: Urban Lichen & Patina Reconnaissance
quests.objective: Identify colonies of crustose or foliose lichen colonizing stone, brick, or metal surfaces.
quests.suitability_reason: Air quality bio-indicators accessible in every neighborhood; requires only patient observation.

steps.instruction: Inspect sunlit stone walls, concrete benches, or wooden posts in your neighborhood.
steps.detail: Look for circular, textured patches of yellow, mint green, or grey.

steps.instruction: Examine the boundary where lichen meets bare stone.
steps.detail: Observe the crust-like adherence without scraping or peeling the organism.

steps.instruction: Compare lichen on a sheltered northern exposure versus a southern sun-baked wall.
steps.detail: Notice differences in thickness and hue.

checklist: Found at least one circular lichen colony on a hard surface
Noticed color variations between damp and dry sectors
Checked a wooden pole or stone wall for symbiotic growth
quests.bonus_challenge: Estimate the diameter of the largest colony you observe.
quests.safe_alternative: Inspect exterior window masonry or patio tiles from an indoor vantage point.
quests.completion_criteria: Confirm the presence of one distinct lichen organism.
quests.reflection_question: How old do you imagine that slow-growing lichen colony might be?
safety_notes: Do not scratch or remove lichens; they grow at rates of fractions of a millimeter per year.
Stay clear of active construction sites.
